name: Answyr
author: Kevon Adonis

sections.description:
Answyr is AI-powered customer support for WordPress, end to end — from
self-serve AI chat that deflects common questions to AI-assisted replies that help
your agents respond faster. It all runs on one shared AI core, grounded in a
knowledge base you own and control.

  • AI Chat — a front-end deflection widget that answers visitors from your knowledge base (with source links) and escalates into a ticket when a human is needed.
  • Knowledge Base — a built-in, customizable knowledge base that grounds every AI answer. Keep it internal for the AI and your agents, or publish it for customers with a shortcode.
  • AI-assisted agent replies — an AI ticket inbox (Desk) that drafts replies grounded in your knowledge base, with a full ticket lifecycle and a customer portal.

Every feature is free. There is no paid version. Bring your own AI provider key (Anthropic or OpenAI). Keys are encrypted at rest.

Features

  • Ticket lifecycle — two statuses, open and resolved. Each open ticket shows whose turn it is (waiting on you or on the customer); a customer reply reopens a resolved ticket, and customers can resolve or reopen from the portal.
  • Triage — priority (low/normal/high/urgent), free-form tags, status/priority/tag filters, keyword search, pagination. The inbox is ordered urgent-first.
  • Productivity — AI draft-and-vet, saved (canned) replies, macros (one click sets the reply, status and tags), internal team-only notes, ⌘/Ctrl+Enter to send.
  • AI helpers — suggest tags and priority, summarize a long thread, polish a rough reply, turn a resolved ticket into a draft help article, and a brand voice for AI replies and chat answers.
  • Attachments — agents and customers can attach files to tickets. Files are stored privately and served only through a permission-checked link.
  • Customer portal — inline sign-in, create/see/reply to tickets, Open/Resolved filter, 👍/👎 satisfaction (CSAT) on resolved tickets.
  • Chat deflection widget — answers from your knowledge base with source links, and escalates to a ticket (with transcript) when needed. Customizable title, welcome copy, placeholder, accent color, and display mode (sitewide or shortcode).
  • Brand theming — an accent color themes the chat widget and the customer portal; admin screens stay native.
  • Insights — ticket volume, new tickets (7/30 days), average first-response time, satisfaction, and a by-status breakdown. For chat: deflection rate, top questions, transcripts, and a documentation-gap report listing the questions your knowledge base couldn’t answer.
  • Customizable knowledge base — a native knowledge base grounds every AI draft and chat answer; internal by default, publishable to customers. You can also point the AI at existing content (any post types you choose).

AI providers

Anthropic and OpenAI ship built-in. You configure your own API key per provider
and choose the active provider/model in settings. The architecture is
multi-provider by design, so additional providers can be registered.

External services

Answyr sends data to a third-party AI provider only when you have
enabled an AI feature (draft-and-vet or the Chat widget) and configured that
provider’s API key. It is “bring your own key” — no AI calls are made until you
add a key, and only the provider you select as active is contacted.

What is sent, and when:

  • When an agent uses an AI feature (a suggested reply, polish, triage, a thread summary, or a help-article draft), or a visitor asks the Chat widget a question, the plugin sends the relevant ticket/conversation text and excerpts of your own published content used for grounding to the active AI provider, and receives a generated reply.

Which service: the provider you configure as active —

  • Anthropic (Claude) — used when Anthropic is the active provider. Requests go to api.anthropic.com.
    Terms: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms
    Privacy policy: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • OpenAI — used when OpenAI is the active provider. Requests go to api.openai.com.
    Terms: https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use
    Privacy policy: https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy

No data is sent to these services unless you enable an AI feature and provide a key.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the answyr folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install via the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin. This creates the ticket tables and seeds defaults.
  3. Go to Answyr → Settings, choose an AI provider, and paste your API key.
  4. Enable the surfaces you want (Desk is on by default; Chat is off until configured).
  5. Add the [answyr_portal] shortcode to a page for the customer portal, and [answyr_chat] if you use shortcode display for the chat widget.

Requires WordPress 6.0+ and PHP 8.0+.
sections.faq:
Does the AI send replies automatically?

No. Every AI-generated reply is a draft that a human reviews and sends. Nothing is sent to a customer automatically.

Do I need an AI provider account?

Yes — Answyr is bring-your-own-key. You add your own Anthropic or OpenAI API key. No AI calls are made until a key is configured.

Where are my API keys stored?

Keys are stored per-provider and encrypted at rest in your site’s database.

What data leaves my site?

Only when you use an AI feature: the ticket/conversation text and excerpts of your own published content used for grounding are sent to your chosen AI provider. See the “External services” section above.

Does Answyr store chat conversations?

Yes, in your own site’s database, so Insights can show deflection, top questions and documentation gaps. Conversations older than 90 days are deleted automatically. Nothing is sent to us.

Will uninstalling remove my data?

Not unless you ask it to. By default, deleting the plugin keeps your tickets, settings and keys, so reinstalling picks up where you left off. To erase everything instead, choose “Remove everything” under Settings → Advanced before deleting. Knowledge-base posts are always kept.
sections.changelog:
1.3.2 – 2026-11-24

A redesigned ticket page, a sortable ticket list with unread dots, and a clearer portal for signed-out visitors.

  • New: The ticket list shows a dot next to tickets with a customer message nobody has opened yet. Opening the ticket clears it for your whole team, and a new reply from the customer brings it back. Existing tickets start as read.
  • New: Sort the ticket list by any column. It now shows the most recently updated tickets first.
  • Improved: A redesigned ticket page: a header with previous/next, the conversation beside a sidebar for the customer, status, tags, files and AI tools, and one reply box with Reply and Internal note tabs. Long conversations fold their middle messages so the latest stay in view.
  • Improved: A cleaner ticket list header: view tabs with counts, and one toolbar for bulk actions, filters and search.
  • Improved: When guest requests are on, signed-out visitors choose between Sign in and Continue as guest tabs on the portal.
  • Changed: Guest requests from the portal now need a subject.
  • Fixed: Ticket and message times could be hours off when your database server and your site use different time zones, which also skewed the average first response time in Insights. Times are now stored in your site’s time zone, and existing ones are converted once when you update.

1.3.1 – 2026-11-23

Simpler ticket statuses, and automated emails no longer become tickets.

  • Changed: Tickets now have two statuses, Open and Resolved. Pending and Closed are gone: your existing Pending tickets become Open and Closed tickets become Resolved. Open tickets still show whose turn it is.
  • New: Email to tickets ignores automated senders. No-reply, mailer-daemon and bounce addresses never open a ticket, and Settings → Tickets → Email → Ignore mail from lets you add your own (an address, billing@, or a domain like @stripe.com).

1.3.0 – 2026-11-23

Every feature is now free: macros, attachments, chat history and analytics, and the AI helpers.

  • New: Macros, file attachments, chat transcripts and analytics (including the documentation-gap report), and the AI helpers (triage, summaries, polish, help-article drafts, brand voice) are now part of Answyr for everyone. There is no paid version anymore.
  • Changed: Removed the upgrade prompts and the licensing library.
  • Moving from Answyr Pro? Deactivate Answyr Pro, then activate this plugin. Your tickets, settings and attachments carry over. Before deleting Answyr Pro, check that Settings → Advanced is set to keep tickets and settings.

1.2.0 – 2026-11-23

Customers can open a ticket from your support portal without signing in.

  • New: Turn on Settings → Tickets → Guest requests and visitors can send a request from the portal with just their name, email and question, plus any intake fields you ask for. They get the usual confirmation email and replies by email. If the email belongs to an existing account, the request shows up in that customer’s portal when they sign in. Switched on for new installs; existing sites keep sign-in only until you turn it on.
  • New: Delete tickets you no longer need, one at a time or in bulk from the ticket list. Administrators only.
  • New: A Support Assistant can save a suggested reply on a ticket for you to review, edit and send. Find them under Drafts to review in the ticket list.
  • Improved: The support form and the portal now have a hidden spam trap and sensible length limits on what visitors can send.

1.1.3 – 2026-10-31

Your tickets and settings stay put when the plugin is deleted.

  • Improved: Deleting Answyr now keeps your tickets and settings, so reinstalling picks up right where you left off.
  • New: Choose what happens when Answyr is deleted under Settings → Advanced: keep tickets and settings (the default), or remove everything.
  • New: The Plugins screen shows what deleting Answyr will do. If you have a spare copy installed, such as the free version left behind after installing Pro, deleting it asks first what to do with your tickets and settings.

1.1.2 – 2026-10-31

Tickets by email, and a safe way to connect outside tools to your Desk.

  • New: Tickets by email. Connect Postmark, Mailgun, SendGrid or Resend to your support address and new emails become tickets, while customers’ replies land back in their ticket. Out-of-office replies and duplicates are ignored. Set it up under Settings → Tickets → Email.
  • Improved: With email turned on, customers can simply reply to Answyr’s emails instead of being told replies are not monitored.
  • New: A Support Assistant user role that can read tickets and add internal notes, but cannot reply to customers or change anything else. Give it to an outside tool, such as an AI assistant that drafts replies for you to review, through an application password.
  • New: Developers can read a ticket’s full thread over the REST API, and page and search the ticket list.

1.1.1 – 2026-08-13

  • New: Existing Answyr Pro customers can now activate their license from the free plugin — an “Activate a license” option on Settings → AI and the Insights upgrade prompt opens Freemius’s activation screen and installs the Pro version automatically.

1.1.0 – 2026-07-25

New free features across Desk + Chat, plus the first premium tier (Answyr Pro).

  • New: Configurable intake fields — ask customers for their website, versions, and setup on the support form and portal; each ticket shows a “Customer context” panel, and the AI draft uses it.
  • New: The agent reply box is now the full WordPress editor (rich formatting), with matching HTML customer emails and portal replies.
  • New: Unresolved-ticket count badge on the Answyr admin menu.
  • New: “Waiting on” indicator — tickets and the inbox show Pending agent response / Pending customer response from the last reply.
  • New: Chat transcripts attached to a ticket are styled by speaker (customer vs agent).
  • Improved: Clearer AI answers — no “Based on the documentation” preface, and chat points customers to open a support ticket instead of naming an outside company.
  • Improved: Settings → API Keys nudges you to Save after a successful key test, and warns before you leave with an unsaved key.
  • New (Pro): Chat analytics & documentation-gap report — deflection rates, top questions, and the exact questions your knowledge base couldn’t answer (ranked, so you know which docs to write next).
  • New (Pro): Macros — one-click reply + status + tags.
  • New (Pro): File attachments on tickets and replies — stored privately and served only through a permission-checked, signed link.
  • New (Pro): AI power-ups — auto-triage (suggested tags & priority), thread summaries, brand voice for AI replies & chat, “turn a resolved ticket into a draft help-center article,” and Polish reply (clean up an agent’s rough draft).

1.0.0 – 2026-07-13

Initial public release.

  • AI Chat — a front-end deflection widget that answers visitors from your knowledge base with source links, and escalates into a ticket (with transcript) when a human is needed. Customizable title, welcome copy, placeholder, accent color, and display mode.
  • Knowledge Base — a native, customizable knowledge base that grounds every AI answer. Internal by default; publish it for customers with the [answyr_kb] shortcode. You can also ground the AI on existing content (post types you choose).
  • Desk — an AI ticket inbox with AI draft-and-vet replies, a full lifecycle (open → pending → resolved → closed), triage (priority, tags, filters, keyword search), saved replies, internal notes, and an Insights dashboard.
  • Customer portal — inline sign-in; create, view, and reply to tickets; Open/Closed filter; 👍/👎 satisfaction on resolved tickets. Themed by your accent color.
  • Bring your own AI provider key — Anthropic or OpenAI, encrypted at rest. No AI calls are made until you add a key.
